feat(phase-5): implement createAgentWallet with real validator CBORs

validators.ts (new):
- Extracts AGENT_WALLET_CBOR and THREAD_TOKEN_BASE_CBOR from plutus.json
- Documents the source path for each so they're easy to regenerate

index.ts (rewrite):
- createAgentWallet: picks seed UTxO, applies it as parameter to the
  thread_token minting policy via applyParamsToScript, derives unique
  policyId, mints 1 thread token, locks initial ADA + token at script
  address in one atomic tx

  (guards against attacker-planted UTxOs with fake datums)

docs: add and accept ADR-0005 (S3 patterns as canonical protocol vocabulary)

S3 is the canonical pattern vocabulary for flyway's consent and governance
surface. Adoption proceeds in three phased tiers — Tier 1 (protocol
primitives in flyway-core) is the next implementation milestone, with
seven specific patterns scoped against §IV.1 and §IV.7 of the bundled
Practical Guide. Tier 2 (agent skills) and Tier 3 (reference docs) are
future work with candidates named but artifact decisions deferred.

License conventions for CC BY-SA derivatives spelled out.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: add S3 Practical Guide as canonical reference for sociocracy work

Bundles the official Sociocracy 3.0 Practical Guide (Bockelbrink, Priest,
David — v2026-01-26) into docs/concepts/. This becomes flyway's canonical
S3 source: any flyway tool, skill, instruction, or governance primitive
derived from S3 cites this edition, and if our description and the guide
disagree, the guide wins.

Updated sociocracy-3.md and consent-mechanisms.md to point at the local
PDF. Added an explicit license note: S3 is CC BY-SA 4.0, flyway is MIT,
so any derivative content (paraphrased patterns, S3-derived agent
instructions) needs to carry CC BY-SA attribution while pattern names
and factual references can stay MIT.

S3 Practical Guide is © James Priest, Bernhard Bockelbrink, Liliana
David — CC BY-SA 4.0. Bundled here under that license.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs: add docs/concepts/ — Source, S3, and consent-mechanisms primers

The README and protocol use "Source" in the precise Koenig/Nixon sense, and
adopt S3 consent as the default decision-making framework. These are
load-bearing concepts; readers shouldn't have to reverse-engineer them from
the ADRs or the research synthesis.

- defining-source.md: what Source means (Peter Koenig and Tom Nixon's work)
  with reading list
- sociocracy-3.md: brief S3 primer, Bockelbrink/Priest/David, and a pointer
  to the open Practical Guide
- consent-mechanisms.md: the five flyway decision rules (s3-consent,
  lazy-consent, dual-source-sign, weighted-vote-bounded, apache-vote) and
  the four invariants that are never pluggable

README: inline definition of Source at first use with a link out to the
new primer; docs/concepts/ added to the repository layout map.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

docs+core: reframe from "no joint action" to consent achievement

The defensive framing inherited from the research paper ("when Sources do not
agree, the correct outcome is no joint action") collapsed flyway's whole
constructive purpose into its endpoint. flyway IS a mechanism for achieving
consent — surfacing objections, integrating concerns, running the response
cycle. It is NOT a mechanism for forcing agreement. That distinction is
load-bearing. Exit is the end of a good-faith consent-seeking process, not
a substitute for one.

Updated in four places for consistency:
- README: new "What flyway Is For" section naming consent achievement as
  the positive purpose; mentions the actual primitives (proposals,
  objections, decision rules, escalation ladder)
- flyway-core protocol instructions: invariants reframed from "no joint
  action without consent" to "seek consent; never force it" and "exit
  follows process, not impatience"
- flyway_respond tool description: names the consent cycle explicitly;
  decision enum positions exit as the end of a process
- ADR-0004: incidental "no joint action" reference replaced with "consent cycle"

Research paper §1.2 / §10.4 remain as the historical snapshot they are.
